question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay for config/tool/system defaults, or keep immutable baseline checks in conformance-only Policy surfaces?
rationale: This choice changes the security boundary, config precedence, diagnostics, and upgrade behavior; code inspection shows current main has partial protections but no canonical immutable overlay contract.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, tests, and docs.

options.title: Keep Policy conformance-only
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy/Nix-style external management for audits while runtime config remains the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer until hook work settles
options.body: Leave this issue open while related policy-hook proposals establish the plugin enforcement context needed for a narrower design.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the issue and authored the prior implementation candidate, making them the clearest decision owner for the security boundary.
